title: Calculating kinetic energy
keyIdea: Kinetic energy KE = ½ m v² with mass in kg and speed in m/s, giving joules. Square the speed, keep the half, and rearrange with v = √(2 KE / m). Doubling speed multiplies KE by four because of v².
familyTip: Ask: a 60 kg cyclist at 5 m/s — what is KE? Then: if speed doubles, does energy double or quadruple?

visual.caption: KE calculation idea or mix-up? Drag each clue, or tap it then a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: reveal KE = ½mv², calculate 750 J, show the v² four-times rule, rearrange for speed, catch mix-ups, then challenge.

kid: Moving things have kinetic energy. The formula is KE = ½ m v². Mass m is in kilograms and speed v is in metres per second. The answer is in joules (J).
Work carefully: square the speed first, multiply by the mass, then multiply by one half. Example: 60 kg at 5 m/s → ½ × 60 × 25 = 750 J.
Because of the v², doubling the speed multiplies the energy by four. Tripling the speed multiplies it by nine. Mass only scales the energy once.
To find speed from energy and mass, rearrange: v = √(2 KE / m). Take the positive root for speed.
adult: Ages 14 to 16. GCSE Energy / NGSS HS-PS3-1: calculate and rearrange KE = ½mv² with coherent SI units. This is the calculation lesson; the mass–speed dependence demo is the related conceptual topic.

Words: kinetic energy, joule, mass, speed, square, rearrange, square root. Common mistakes: forgetting the ½; not squaring v; using KE = mv; thinking doubling speed only doubles KE; mixing grams with m/s.
In the lab the learner reveals the formula, computes 750 J, sees the four-times rule, solves for v, spots the double-speed myth, and orders the method.

practice.explain: The kinetic energy formula is KE = ½ m v². Products of mass and speed, or sums, are wrong.

practice.prompt: m = {a} kg, v = {b} m/s. KE in J?
practice.hint: Square the speed, multiply by mass, then by one half.

practice.prompt: If speed doubles and mass stays the same, KE…
practice.explain: v² means (2v)² = 4v², so kinetic energy becomes four times as large.

practice.prompt: m = {a} kg at 4 m/s. KE in J?

practice.hint: Spot the false claim about doubling speed.
practice.explain: Because of v², doubling speed multiplies KE by four, not two.

pool.prompt: Units of KE from kg and m/s are…
pool.hint: Name the energy unit from mass and speed.
pool.explain: With mass in kg and speed in m/s, KE is in joules.

pool.prompt: To find speed from KE and mass use…
pool.hint: Rearrange KE = ½mv² for v carefully.
pool.explain: Multiply by 2, divide by m, then take the square root.

pool.hint: Square v, then multiply by half the mass.
Square the scale factor on speed.
pool.explain: (3v)² = 9v², so kinetic energy becomes nine times as large.

pool.prompt: Forgetting the ½ in KE = ½mv²…
pool.hint: What does dropping the half do to the value?
pool.explain: Leaving out ½ makes the calculated energy twice as large as it should be.

pool.prompt: KE = {a} J and m = 2 kg. What is v²?
pool.hint: From KE = ½mv² with m = 2, KE = v², so v² equals KE.
